AI is running inside a quarter of your business tasks — and almost certainly not changing how the business actually works.

SAP's global research with Oxford Economics, published October 14, delivers two numbers every executive should internalize. Organizations are already using AI across approximately 25% of business tasks. Yet only 9% of organizations have fundamentally adapted their business around AI.

That is not an adoption problem. It is an integration architecture problem. Companies have deployed AI into existing workflows without rethinking the workflows themselves. The result is automation layered on top of legacy process logic — faster execution of decisions that may no longer make sense.

The 9% that have adapted are not just using AI differently. They are organized differently. Their operating models, decision rights, data governance, and performance metrics have been restructured around what AI makes possible rather than what humans used to do manually.

This gap will widen. As AI capabilities compound — multimodal reasoning, autonomous agents, real-time decision systems — the distance between companies that bolted AI onto old processes and companies that rebuilt processes around AI will become the primary competitive differentiator in every sector.

The question is no longer whether to adopt AI. It is whether your organization's operating model is designed to extract value from the AI you have already deployed.
